messages:
Marie: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposing a hybrid pattern: keep the control plane logically shared but move tenant-specific control traffic (agent handshakes, telemetry, rollout commands) through a per-tenant relay agent in the customer's VPC instead of full VPC peering. Thoughts?

Ajay: Curious, what's the main driver? cost of peering or operational isolation?

Marie: Both. Peering multiplies route tables + cross-account NAT complexity. Relay keeps egress minimal, avoids lots of peering routes, and we can use short-lived mTLS tunnels.

Tony: How do we handle cert distribution for the per-tenant relays? KMS/HSM integration?

Marie: Plan A: use our central CA to mint node certs with limited lifetime, delivered via the control plane at onboarding. Plan B: customers can supply their own certs if they want (BYO).

Sara: What about reachability for canary rollouts? If relay is one-way (egress from tenant -> our control plane), can we push commands reliably?

Marie: Relay maintains a persistent mTLS websocket back to control plane. Commands are sent over that channel. If it drops, we fallback to a short-poll via signed webhook.

Kyle: Sounds fine but what about NAT preservation for source-IP related policies? Some customers rely on original source IP for egress filtering. If we proxy, we break that.

Ajay: We could support a passthrough mode where the relay sets up a 1:1 SNAT mapping to preserve source addresses for specific subnets. More ops complexity though.

Tony: Ops complexity + billing implications. Also need to think about metrics: per-tenant telemetry accuracy must not be blurred by centralized proxies.

Sara: Can we keep prefix/KV cache local to the relay so generation latency doesn't spike? e.g., cache recent KV entries and small batching at the relay level.

Marie: Yes, relay will maintain a bounded KV cache and apply local batching heuristics. We'll expose tunable params in the agent config: max_batch_ms, kv_cache_size.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New spike branch created: rfcs/hybrid-relay-2026. See: https://git.internal/rfcs/348 (deploy log attached)

Kyle: Security question — if customer wants air-gapped control plane, relay plus peering? hybrid becomes messy. Are we saying hybrid is not meant for air-gapped customers?

Marie: Correct. Air-gapped customers require Private deployment or explicit peering with our private control plane. Hybrid relay is for customers who want to avoid full peering but still want near-real-time control with minimal network footprint.

Ajay: Latency SLOs? If relay is in customer's region, tail latency should be fine. Need to document worst-case path: relay -> controlplane region failover -> fallback via webhook.

Tony: Can we include a small config snippet in the RFC for relay agent bootstrap? e.g.:
```
agent:
  mode: relay
  bootstrap: https://cp.example/redwood/bootstrap
  cert_ttl: 6h
  kv_cache_size: 128MB
  max_batch_ms: 50
```

Sara: +1 to adding a bootstrap snippet. Also add troubleshooting: how to verify mTLS (openssl s_client example) and how to rotate certs.

Marie: Good call. I'll add sections: "bootstrap example", "cert lifecycle", "latency SLOs", "ops tradeoffs (SNAT vs passthrough)" and a short migration plan for customers on peering today.

Kyle: Migration plan note: we need a dual-run window where both peering and relay are active until customers switch. That means config flags on control plane to prefer relay channels.

Ajay: For cost modelling, include estimated egress bandwidth cost delta and operational runbook complexity. Keep an appendix with cost formulas.

Marie: Will do. I'll update the RFC branch and ping the list when it's ready for an ops readiness review. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: remind-bot: Reminder set for 3 days to request ops review on rfcs/hybrid-relay-2026
